methodSelector.label: Method
methodSelector.adaptiveDescription: Our adaptive lens for M&A. We blend EV/EBITDA multiples with DCF (and NAV when asset-heavy) and pick the weights based on your business profile — owner-led SMEs lean on multiples + SDE, profitable mid-market blends cash flow and multiples, asset-heavy cases anchor on the balance sheet. Pick this when you're not sure which method fits, or for a market-defensible starting point before setting your own weights.
methodSelector.ebitdaMultipleDescription: Market approach on EV/EBITDA. Best fit for profitable SMEs with ≥2 years of stabilised EBITDA. We triangulate a sector multiple (P25/P75) and apply size and illiquidity discounts. Combinable with DCF and NAV in a weighted synthesis.
methodSelector.revenueMultipleDescription: Market approach on EV/Revenue. Use when EBITDA is negative, unstable or irrelevant (growth companies, recent funding rounds, strong seasonality). The business-type selection sets the sector multiple band and revenue-quality factors (recurrence, churn, top-customer concentration).
methodSelector.combinableHint: Pick one or more methods to include in your weighted synthesis.
methodSelector.exclusivityHint: SDE and EV/EBITDA cannot be combined. Revenue-based methods count as one method.
methodSelector.arrMultipleDescription: ARR lens for SaaS. Business model and type control which SaaS metrics are shown.
methodSelector.dcfDescription: Income approach for businesses with ≥2 years of revenue and EBITDA. Smart defaults from your history (CAGR, margin, sector WACC band), live FCFF preview, ±1pp sensitivity matrix. Pre-revenue? Use Startup Valuation instead.
methodSelector.adjustedNavDescription: Defensible floor value: book equity revalued to fair market on a per-asset basis (real estate, hidden reserves, equipment, off-balance items) net of latent corporate tax. Best for asset-heavy SMEs and holding companies; combines with multiples or DCF in weighted synthesis at 10–30%.
methodSelector.sdeMultipleDescription: For micro-SMEs and sole proprietorships (revenue < €5M). Adds owner salary back to EBITDA.
methodSelector.fiscal4xDescription: Reference calculation for a possible capital-gains acquisition value under BE Art. 90 WIB 92. Forfait formula = Equity + 4× EBITDA of the last closed fiscal year. The final tax position, rate, conditions and applicable acquisition-value anchors must be confirmed with a tax advisor.
methodSelector.startupValuationDescription: Venture-grade Berkus + Scorecard + VC blend for pre-revenue and early-stage founders. No historical financials needed—qualitative milestones, traction, SAFEs and cap-table only.
methodSelector.liquidationAnalysisDescription: Asset-based downside lens. Orderly wind-down (6–12 months) and forced auction scenarios per Pratt & Niculita (2008). The floor value an owner could realistically recover if the business cannot be sold as a going concern. Same balance-sheet inputs as Adjusted NAV.
methodSelector.fiscalDisclaimerText: Forfait formula (Art. 90 WIB 92) for a possible capital-gains acquisition-value reference. Confirm the final acquisition value, applicable anchors and tax treatment with a tax advisor.

fieldHints.dcfNwcPct: NWC ratio as a percentage of revenue. The FCFF bridge subtracts only the yearly change: ratio × revenue growth, with a negative value when working capital is released.
fieldHints.dcfWaccSummary: WACC is the blended discount rate for future cash flows: it weights the cost of equity and after-tax cost of debt. Expand the breakdown to tune inputs.
fieldHints.saasArr: Your annual recurring revenue — the predictable subscription income over 12 months.
fieldHints.saasMrr: Monthly recurring revenue. Auto-filled as ARR / 12 when you enter ARR.
fieldHints.saasArrGrowthPct: Annual (year-over-year) growth of your ARR. High growth (>30% YoY) significantly increases multiples.
fieldHints.saasChurnPct: Percentage of recurring revenue lost from existing customers in the last 12 months.
fieldHints.saasCustomerChurnPct: Percentage of customers who cancelled in the last 12 months.
fieldHints.saasNrrPct: How much revenue you retain and expand from existing customers (including upsells). Above 110% is strong.
fieldHints.saasGrossMarginPct: Revenue minus cost of goods sold, divided by revenue. SaaS typically 70–85%.
fieldHints.saasCac: Customer Acquisition Cost — average cost to acquire one new customer.
fieldHints.saasSmSpend: Total sales & marketing spend in the last 12 months. Used to calculate Magic Number.
fieldHints.saasCustomerConcentrationPct: Revenue share of your largest customer. Above 30% signals concentration risk.
fieldHints.saasExpansionRevenuePct: Extra revenue from upsells and cross-sells to existing customers. High expansion drives NRR above 100%.

navPanels.upliftsDescription: Mark balance-sheet items above book value: real estate, hidden reserves, intangibles. Positive amounts grow the gross corrections AND the tax-latency base.

fields.sdeSalaryPrefilledFromLedger: Prefilled from your trial balance (account 620, FY {year}). Edit if needed.
fields.sdeSalaryPrefilledFromNormalization: Prefilled from an accepted salary normalization (FY {year}). Edit if needed.
fields.sdeOwnerRoleWorkingDesc: Buyer hires a replacement → SDE add-back is excess pay vs. market.
fields.sdeOwnerRolePassiveDesc: No replacement needed → full salary + benefits add back.
fields.sdeActiveOwnersHelp: Engine applies a key-person discount when only one owner runs the business. Range 1–5.
fields.sdeRevenueCapBlock: SDE is intended for businesses under €5M revenue. Above that cap, pick EBITDA × multiple instead.
fields.sdeNonPositiveEbitdaBlock: SDE needs positive EBITDA from the latest complete year. Add EBITDA history above, or pick a different method.
fields.navRealEstateAdjustmentDesc: Current market value of real estate minus book value. Use a recent appraisal or estimate.
fields.navRealEstateAdjustmentFromAppraisal: Derived from your book → appraisal entries below — edit those to change this number.
fields.navInventoryAdjustmentDesc: Adjustment to net realisable value: selling price minus costs to sell.
fields.navHiddenReservesDesc: Difference between book value and fair value of assets not captured elsewhere (e.g. brands, software, customer base).
fields.navGoodwillWriteoffDesc: Write-off of acquired goodwill that is no longer realistic. Reduces total assets.
fields.navReceivablesAdjustmentDesc: Correction for uncollectable or doubtful debts. Usually a negative amount.
fields.navOtherRevaluationsDesc: Revaluation of participations, machinery, vehicles, or other assets not covered by the categories above.
fields.navTaxLatencyPctDesc: Corporate tax on realised capital gains. Belgian default is 25%. On shares often 0% (participation exemption).
fields.navOffBalanceItemsDesc: Obligations not on the balance sheet: pending legal claims, environmental liabilities, severance arrangements, etc.
fields.navPerAssetTaxRatesDescription: Override the global rate for individual asset classes when relevant: BE participation exemption (real-estate share = 0%), recoverable VAT on doubtful receivables, tax-loss carryforwards, etc. Blank fields fall back to the global rate above.
fields.navLead: Revalue the balance sheet to a more realistic market view. This helps estimate a defendable floor value for the business.
fields.navQuickStart: A strong first pass is real estate revaluation, hidden reserves, receivables, and any off-balance obligations.
fields.saasLead: Use this section only for software or SaaS companies. Start with the recurring revenue inputs first, then add retention and efficiency metrics if you know them.
fields.saasQuickStart: You do not need every field. A solid first pass is ARR, ARR growth, NRR, and optionally MRR.
fields.saasDerivedNeedMoreInputs: Add ARR plus at least two more SaaS inputs to make the derived metrics more reliable.
fields.revenueQualityLead: Enter the key revenue-quality inputs below. These help the engine calibrate the applied multiple.
fields.revRecurringCurrencyDescription: Annual amount from subscriptions, contracts, or recurring customers
fields.revTopClientCurrencyTooltip: Sum the revenue of your 3 largest clients. High concentration increases risk profile and reduces the multiple.
fields.revContractBacklogDescription: Total value of signed but not yet executed contracts
fields.revGrossChurnTooltip: What percentage of last year's recurring revenue was lost to cancellations? (SaaS standard is 5–10%)
fields.revenueQualityPreviewFootnote: Preview ratios from your latest full-year revenue. The engine still uses the raw inputs directly.
fields.ebitdaQualityLead: Enter the key EBITDA-quality inputs below. These help the engine calibrate the applied multiple.
fields.revTopClientCurrencyEbitdaTooltip: Sum the revenue of the 3 largest clients. Loss of a major client can wipe out the entire EBITDA margin when fixed costs are high.
fields.revCapitalizedRdDescription: Amount of software development costs capitalized on the balance sheet last year. The engine deducts this to show Cash EBITDA.
fields.navPreviewFootnote: Estimated correction based on entered fields. The full corrected NAV is computed by the engine with balance-sheet data.
fields.navSynthesisHint: Used as floor value in synthesis (weight 10–30%)
fields.navEstimatedNavUnavailable: Enter balance-sheet data (total assets and liabilities) to show estimated NAV.
fields.navBookEquityAnchorHint: Total assets − total liabilities from your latest balance sheet.
fields.fiscalPreviewFootnote: 4× EBITDA anchor matches Belgian fiscal reference; ownership multiplier may differ in the full run.
fields.fiscalPreviewEbitdaBasisWeighted: EBITDA here is the same weighted normalized historical EBITDA as in step 3 — aligned with the report and fiscal annex (not the raw single-year figure).
fields.fiscalPreviewOwnershipStakeHint: Matches omni: (book + anchor) × (shares for sale ÷ 100). Manual flow keeps 100% stake unless the product exposes partial stakes later.
fields.fiscalPreviewFormulaA11y: Formula: fiscal anchor plus book equity equals implied reference equity.
fields.fiscalPreviewUnavailableNonBe: Fiscal reference applies to Belgian companies (company country).
fields.fiscalPreviewUnavailableEbitda: Positive EBITDA is required for the 4× anchor.
fields.fiscalPreviewUnavailableMissingEbitda: Add a complete historical year with EBITDA to preview the fiscal anchor.
fields.fiscalPreviewUnavailableMissingEquity: Book equity is missing for the latest complete year. The 4× anchor still shows; the full statutory-style reference equity (book + 4× EBITDA) needs balance-sheet lines.
fields.fiscalPreviewMissingEquityAction: In Financial history, add totals for that year: equity, or assets and liabilities (or assets and debt) so book equity can be derived.

chatAssistant.qualityCtaThinComparablesPrompt: The industry multiple is based on a thin or proxy-sector dataset. Help me confirm the business type is correctly classified, and if not propose a better classification or a manual multiple override.
chatAssistant.qualityCtaOwnerConcentrationPrompt: The owner-concentration adjustment was skipped because number of owners or employees is missing. Help me fill these in so the discount is applied correctly.
chatAssistant.qualityCtaEbitdaDivergencePrompt: The reported EBITDA and the normalized EBITDA in the metadata disagree. Walk me through the normalizations so both numbers line up before the report is shared.
chatAssistant.qualityCtaMethodSubstitutionPrompt: The requested valuation method could not be executed fully and was substituted. Help me fill the missing inputs so I can run the originally selected method correctly or explicitly document why the substitute method is appropriate.
chatAssistant.qualityCtaEbitdaBenchmarkDeviationPrompt: The EBITDA margin deviates materially from the sector median. Help me document the cause (owner compensation, one-offs, or structural difference) and add a targeted normalization line where needed.
chatAssistant.qualityCtaNetDebtPrompt: No balance-sheet data was provided so net debt was assumed to be zero and the operating-cash exemption used a revenue proxy. Help me add cash, total debt, and current liabilities so the EV→Equity bridge becomes audit-defensible.
chatAssistant.qualityCtaOwnerCompEstimatedPrompt: Owner compensation was estimated instead of explicitly provided. Help me enter the actual amount (or market replacement cost) so normalized EBITDA is defensible.
chatAssistant.qualityCtaBookEquityPrompt: Book equity is missing, so the Belgian fiscal-reference calculation cannot fully close. Help me add total equity (or total assets and total debt) from the latest filed accounts.
chatAssistant.qualityCtaImpossibleMarginPrompt: One or more years show a normalised EBITDA margin ≥ 100% — mathematically impossible for an operating entity. Help me identify the cause: (1) a mapping error on the EBITDA column, (2) over-aggressive normalisations, or (3) an operating NV with property inside the same entity (in which case the Vastgoed carve-out toggle should likely be enabled).
chatAssistant.qualityTitleThinComparables: Sector multiple drawn from a thin dataset
chatAssistant.qualityBodyThinComparables: The headline multiple is statistically thin on its own. Confirm the business-type classification matches the actual operating model, or override the multiple manually.
chatAssistant.qualityBodyOwnerConcentration: Owner or employee counts were missing, so the concentration discount was not applied. Add them to apply the adjustment.
chatAssistant.qualityBodyEbitdaDivergence: The reported EBITDA and the normalized EBITDA in the metadata don't match. Reconcile the normalizations so both numbers line up before sharing the report.
chatAssistant.qualityBodyMethodSubstitution: The selected method could not run fully with the current data. Add the missing inputs to run it again, or ask the assistant to document why the substitute method is appropriate.
chatAssistant.qualityTitleEbitdaBenchmarkDeviation: Margin is unusual for this sector
chatAssistant.qualityBodyEbitdaBenchmarkDeviation: Capture why the EBITDA margin differs: a normalization, owner compensation, a one-off, or a structural operating difference. That makes the report defensible in discussion.
chatAssistant.qualityTitleNetDebt: Proceeds value is not exact yet
chatAssistant.qualityBodyNetDebt: Cash, financial debt and current liabilities are still missing. Add them to make the bridge from enterprise value to equity value exact.
chatAssistant.qualityBodyOwnerCompEstimated: An explicit owner-compensation figure wasn't supplied, so a market-replacement estimate was used. Enter the actual amount for a fully defensible normalized EBITDA.
chatAssistant.qualityTitleBookEquity: Book equity missing — Belgian fiscal reference partial
chatAssistant.qualityBodyBookEquity: The Belgian fiscal-reference calculation can't fully close without book equity. Add total equity (or total assets + total debt) from the latest filed accounts.
chatAssistant.qualityBodyImpossibleMargin: One or more years show a normalized EBITDA margin at or above revenue, which isn't possible for an operating entity. Check the EBITDA mapping, normalization scope, or enable the Vastgoed carve-out if the entity holds its own property.

methodDescriptions.upswitch_adaptive: Blends the strongest signals from your dossier into one defensible headline equity value.
methodDescriptions.arr_multiple: ARR × an EV/ARR-style multiple, adjusted for NRR, churn, growth, and concentration risk.
methodDescriptions.ebitda_multiple: Normalized EBITDA × a market multiple — standard for trading companies with reliable earnings.
methodDescriptions.omzet_multiple: Revenue × a multiple — useful when margins swing or peers are quoted on sales.
methodDescriptions.revenue_multiple: Revenue × a multiple (same idea as a turnover multiple).
methodDescriptions.sde_multiple: Seller discretionary earnings × a multiple — common for owner-operated SMEs.
methodDescriptions.adjusted_nav: Adjusted net asset value from the balance sheet — floor or anchor for asset-heavy cases; combine with multiples/DCF in synthesis when appropriate.
methodDescriptions.fiscal_4x: Belgian fiscal reference (notional): book equity + 4× normalized EBITDA.
methodDescriptions.dcf: Discounted cash flow (DCF): projects future cash flows and discounts them to today — intrinsic value. Only selectable when the engine can compute DCF (no exclusion); otherwise the reason appears below.
